diagnostic_evidence.quote: e_k = f_k for all $k$, i.e., $A$ and $Q$ have a joint basis of eigenfunctions.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma assumes only Assumption (i) and (ii), but the claim that $\omega_k$ is a standard Wiener process requires $e_k$ to be an eigenfunction of $Q$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_k$. Without (iii), $\operatorname{Var}(\langle W_Q(t),e_k\rangle)=t\langle Q e_k,e_k\rangle$, which need not equal $\lambda_k t$. Thus the standard Wiener statement is false as written; assumption (iii) must be added (or $\omega_k$ must be redefined using $\langle Q e_k,e_k\rangle$).

failure_location.quote: Furthermore the processes $\{\omega_k(t)\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are $\mathbb{R}$-valued, standard Wiener-processes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add Assumption (iii) to the hypotheses for the standard Wiener-process claim, or redefine $\omega_k$ with the correct variance $\langle Q e_k,e_k\rangle$.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's standard Wiener-process claim is unreliable under its stated hypotheses, though the main results that assume (iii) are not directly invalidated.
issues.title: Coefficient lemma omits joint eigenbasis assumption for standard Wiener processes
issues.why_classification: The omission is local; adding (iii) or adjusting the definition fixes the lemma, and the main results already assume (iii).

issues.failure_explanation: From $\xi_k \ge C_\Delta k^{2/d}$ it follows that $(\kappa^2+\xi_k)^\alpha \ge C_\Delta^\alpha k^{2\alpha/d}$ and $(\kappa^2+\xi_k)^{-\beta} \le C_\Delta^{-\beta} k^{-2\beta/d}$. The proof incorrectly replaces $C_\Delta^\alpha$ by $C_\Delta$ and $C_\Delta^{-\beta}$ by $C_\Delta$. Hence the stated constant $C$ is not supported; the correct constant involves $C_\Delta^{-\beta-(2\gamma-1)\alpha}$ (up to other constants).

failure_location.quote: satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the eigenvalue bounds to $\mu_k \ge r^{-1} C_\Delta^\alpha k^{2\alpha/d}$ and $\lambda_k \le \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta^{-\beta} k^{-2\beta/d}$, then recompute $C$.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant in the Laplacian spectral convergence corollary is incorrect, although the convergence rate remains valid.
issues.title: Incorrect constant in Laplacian spectral convergence corollary
issues.why_classification: The error affects only the constant, not the rate or method, and is repaired by a local recalculation.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives a bound on the square root of the expected squared error. To obtain the expected squared error, the right-hand side must be squared: $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$ becomes $\lambda_k$, $\mu_k^{-1/q}$ becomes $\mu_k^{-2/q}$, and the logarithmic factor $\delta_{\gamma,h}$ becomes $\delta_{\gamma,h}^2$ (or the constant must absorb the square). The theorem as stated leaves these factors unsquared, so it can be false for $\lambda_k>1$ and understates the log factor at $\gamma=m+3/2$. The main result's $C''_M$ uses $\lambda_k$, confirming the intended squared version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$ by $\lambda_k$, $\mu_k^{-1/q}$ by $\mu_k^{-2/q}$, and $\delta_{\gamma,h}$ by $\delta_{\gamma,h}^2$ (or redefine the constants accordingly) in the affected results.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal error bounds in Theorem thm-convergence and its corollaries, and the temporal term in Theorem thm:main-result, have incorrect constants and log factors; the convergence rates in $h$ remain correct.
issues.title: Missing square when passing from L2 norm bound to expected squared error
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local squaring of constants and log factors; it preserves all polynomial convergence rates and the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem states a sum, not the square root of the sum. The prose overstates the improvement and misstates the established constant.

failure_location.quote: we can use the second part of \Cref{thm:main-result} to get the improved constant $C_M^{''} = \frac{C}{\Gamma(\gamma)^2} \sqrt{\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-\frac{2}{q}} \lambda_k}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the square root by the sum, matching the theorem's stated $C''_M$.
issues.overall_effect: The discussion misrepresents the size of the temporal error constant and the degeneracy of $Q$ allowed.
issues.title: Prose misstates main-result constant with an extra square root
issues.why_classification: A local correction in the discussion; the formal theorem is the authoritative statement and the convergence rates are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists an $r_{\mu} > 0$ and a $C_1 > 0$ such that $\{\mu_k\}_{k = 1}^\infty$ satisfies $$\mu_k \geq C_1 k^{r_{\mu}}, $$

issues.failure_explanation: A bounded inverse of $A$ means $\sup_k \mu_k^{-1}<\infty$, i.e., $\inf_k \mu_k>0$. It does not imply $\sum_k \mu_k^{-1}<\infty$; the latter is a trace-class condition on $A^{-1}$. For $\mu_k \sim k^{r_\mu}$, the sum converges only if $r_\mu>1$, whereas bounded inverse holds for any $r_\mu>0$.

failure_location.quote: In most practical applications $A$ will have bounded inverse, i.e., $\sum_{k = 1}^M \mu_k^{-1} < \infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Say that $A^{-1}$ is trace class, or impose $\sum_k \mu_k^{-1}<\infty$ as an additional assumption, rather than equating it with bounded inverse.
issues.overall_effect: Misstates the condition under which $C''_M$ is bounded and can mislead about the applicability of the improved constant.
issues.title: Bounded inverse incorrectly identified with summability of eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: A local prose correction; it does not affect the formal convergence results.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor $1/2$ in the formula for $\alpha$: $\alpha = \frac{\nu_s}{2\nu_t} \min(1,\beta_s/\beta^*)$.
issues.overall_effect: The inverse reparametrisation is incorrect; using it generates wrong parameter values and undermines numerical experiments that rely on it.
issues.title: Inverse reparametrisation formula for alpha misses factor one half
issues.why_classification: A local factor correction; the main theory and convergence results are unaffected.
